# Bulk universality for complex eigenvalues of real non-symmetric random matrices with i.i.d. entries

**Authors:** Sofiia Dubova ††thanks: Department of Mathematics, Harvard University, One Oxford Street, Cambridge MA 02138, USA Kevin Yang††footnotemark:

## Abstract

We consider an ensemble of non-Hermitian matrices with independent identically distributed real entries that have finite moments. We show that its $k$ -point correlation function in the bulk away from the real line converges to a universal limit.

## 1 Introduction

Universality of local eigenvalue statistics has long been of interest in random matrix theory. In the case of Hermitian Wigner ensembles this is the content of Wigner-Dyson-Mehta conjecture [24], which was resolved in [17] using a three-step strategy:

- • Local law for the resolvent $G(z)=(H-z)^{-1}$ ;

- • Bulk universality for the perturbed ensemble $H_{t}=H+\sqrt{t}B$ , where $B$ is Gaussian;

- • Comparison of local statistics of $H$ with local statistics of the perturbed matrix $H_{t}$ .

This strategy has since been widely used to show universality of local statistics of other Hermitian ensembles [21, 2]. An established method of carrying out the second step of the strategy for Hermitian ensembles is Dyson Brownian motion (DBM), a system of stochastic differential equations for the eigenvalues of $H_{t}$ . For non-Hermitian random matrices, the natural analogue of DBM involves the left- and right-eigenvector overlaps of the ensemble, which makes its analysis very complicated; see Appendix A in [6], for example. In [11] Cipolloni, Erdős and Schröder side-stepped the non-Hermitian DBM using Girko’s formula [19] to show the universality of local statistics in the edge regime for both complex and real non-Hermitian i.i.d. ensembles. Girko’s formula allows access to the eigenvalue statistics of a non-Hermitian matrix $A$ through the resolvent $G_{z}(\eta)$ of the Hermitization of $A$ :

$$ G_{z}(\eta)=\begin{pmatrix}-i\eta&A-z\\
A^{\ast}-\bar{z}&-i\eta\end{pmatrix}^{-1}. $$

This strategy has not yielded the universality of local statistics in the bulk due to difficulty controlling the correlation of $G_{z_{1}}$ and $G_{z_{2}}$ in the intermediate regime $|z_{1}-z_{2}|\asymp\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}$ . Current techniques only allow to show independence of $G_{z_{1}}$ and $G_{z_{2}}$ in the regime $|z_{1}-z_{2}|>N^{-\frac{1}{2}+\varepsilon}$ , see [14].

Recently, Maltsev and Osman proved bulk universality for complex non-Hermitian i.i.d. matrices in [23] using a different approach based on supersymmetry for the second step of the three-step strategy. They derived an exact integral formula for the $k$ -point correlation function of a random complex non-Hermitian matrix $A$ perturbed by a Gaussian $\sqrt{t}B$ and performed asymptotic analysis to show its convergence to the $k$ -point correlation function of the complex Ginibre ensemble with Gaussian entries. This method was also used to show bulk universality for weakly non-Hermitian complex matrices in [25]. For the purposes of bulk universality, it is enough to take $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ (see Section 7 in [23]), though the analysis in [23] holds until the time-scale $N^{-1/2+\delta}$ assuming the initial data matrix satisfies technical (third-order) local law estimates. (Here, $\epsilon_{0},\delta>0$ are any small parameters independent of $N$ .)

In this work we establish bulk universality for the real non-Hermitian i.i.d. ensemble away from the real line using the strategy of [23]. This builds on [28], in which the first four moments of the entries of $A$ are assumed to match those of the Gaussian distribution. (We note that [28], which builds on the methods in [27] for Hermitian matrices, applies to both real and complex matrix ensembles and both real and complex eigenvalue statistics.) We discuss the additional complications that arise in the real case compared to the complex case after we state our main results.

To be precise, the random matrix ensemble of interest in this paper is given by $A=(A_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{N}$ , where $N\gg 1$ is the matrix size, and $A_{ij}$ are i.i.d. real-valued random variables that satisfy $\mathbb{E}A_{ij}=0$ and $\mathbb{E}|A_{ij}|^{2}=N^{-1}$ and $\mathbb{E}|A_{ij}|^{2p}\lesssim_{p}N^{-p}$ for all $p\geq 1$ . (Throughout this paper, we write $a\lesssim b$ if $|a|\leq C|b|$ , with subscripts to indicate what parameters the constant $C$ depends on.)

Let us now introduce the main objects and constants appearing in this paper.

- • First, we define $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ to be the time-scale of the Gaussian perturbation, where $\epsilon_{0}>0$ is independent of $N$ .

- • For any $z\in\mathbb{C}$ , we define $H_{z}(\eta):=[(A-z)(A-z)^{\ast}+\eta^{2}]^{-1}$ and $\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta):=[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta^{2}]^{-1}$ . We also define the Hermitization $\displaystyle\mathcal{H}_{z}:=\begin{pmatrix}0&A-z\\ A^{\ast}-\overline{z}&0\end{pmatrix}$ and recall the resolvent $G_{z}(\eta)=[\mathcal{H}_{z}-i\eta]^{-1}$ . It turns out (see [23]) that $\displaystyle G_{z}(\eta)=\begin{pmatrix}i\eta H_{z}(\eta)&(A-z)H_{z}(\eta)\\ H_{z}(\eta)(A-z)^{\ast}&i\eta\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta)\end{pmatrix}.$ (1.1)

- • Let $\eta_{z,t}$ solve $t\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\rangle=1$ , where $\langle H\rangle=\frac{1}{\dim H}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}H$ is normalized trace for any square matrix $H$ . See the proof of Theorem 1.1 in [23] for existence and uniqueness of such $\eta_{z,t}$ for $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ (and for the estimate $\frac{1}{C}t\leq\eta_{z,t}\leq Ct$ , which holds whenever the local law in Lemma 26 holds).

- • Set $g_{z,t}=\eta_{z,t}\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\rangle$ and $\alpha_{z,t}=\eta_{z,t}^{2}\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\rangle$ . Set $\beta_{z,t}=\eta_{z,t}\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})^{2}(A-z)\rangle$ and $\gamma_{z,t}=\eta_{z,t}^{2}\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})^{2}\rangle$ . Define $\sigma_{z,t}=\alpha_{z,t}+\gamma_{z,t}^{-1}|\beta_{z,t}|^{2}$ .

Now, recall that the $k$ -point correlation function (for any integer $k\geq 1$ ) of a point process $\{\zeta_{j}\}_{j}$ on $\mathbb{C}$ is the function $\rho(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})$ satisfying

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i_{1}\neq i_{2}\neq\ldots\neq i_{k}}\varphi(\zeta_{i_{1}},\ldots,\zeta_{i_{k}})\right] \displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{C}^{k}}\varphi(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\rho(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})dz_{1}\ldots dz_{k}. $$

The goal of this paper is compute the $k$ -point correlation function in the large $N$ limit for eigenvalues of $A$ in the complex plane, i.e. away from the real line. To state this result precisely, let us fix $k\geq 2$ and define

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{GinUE}}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k}):=\det\left[\frac{1}{\pi}\exp\left\{-\frac{|z_{i}|^{2}+|z_{j}|^{2}}{2}+z_{i}\overline{z}_{j}\right\}\right]_{i,j=1}^{k} $$

This yields essentially the local distribution of $k$ -many eigenvalues for a matrix whose entries are (normalized) complex Gaussians. Remarkably, as we further explain shortly, it also gives the local eigenvalue distribution for real, non-symmetric Gaussian ensembles away from the real line.

#### Theorem 1.

Fix any $k\geq 2$ . For any $O\in C^{\infty}_{c}(\mathbb{C}^{k})$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$ such that $|z|<1$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z)\neq 0$ , we have that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i_{1}\neq i_{2}\neq\ldots\neq i_{k}}O(N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{\mathrm{univ},z}^{\frac{1}{2}}[z-\lambda_{i_{1}}],\ldots,N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{\mathrm{univ},z}^{\frac{1}{2}}[z-\lambda_{i_{k}}])\right] \displaystyle-\int_{\mathbb{C}^{k}}O(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\rho_{\mathrm{univ},z}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})dz_{1}\ldots dz_{k} $$

vanishes as $N\to\infty$ , where $\sigma_{\mathrm{univ},z}>0$ is independent of the distribution of the entries of $A$ , where $\{\lambda_{j}\}_{j}$ are eigenvalues of $A$ , where

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{univ},z}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k}) \displaystyle=\Phi_{z}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\rho_{\mathrm{GinUE}}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k}), $$

and where $\Phi_{z}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})$ is independent of the distribution of the entries of $A$ .

By Theorem 11 in [5], we know $\Phi_{z}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\equiv 1$ , i.e. that local bulk eigenvalue statistics away from the real line agree with those in the complex case. We only stated Theorem 1 in this way to parallel it with Theorem 2. We note a similar analysis of local laws as in Section 7 of [23] shows $\sigma_{\mathrm{univ},z}=1$ , but we omit this extra computation.

The main step in proving Theorem 1 is to first prove the same statement but for matrices with a Gaussian perturbation. In what follows, $B$ is a real Ginibre matrix of size $N\times N$ , i.e. its entries are independent real Gaussians with mean zero and variance $N^{-1}$ .

#### Theorem 2.

Fix any $k\geq 2$ . If we set $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ , then for $\epsilon_{0}>0$ sufficiently small and for any $O\in C^{\infty}_{c}(\mathbb{C}^{k})$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$ such that $|z|<1$ and $\mathrm{Im}(z)\neq 0$ , we have that

$$ \displaystyle\mathbb{E}\left[\sum_{i_{1}\neq i_{2}\neq\ldots\neq i_{k}}O(N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{\frac{1}{2}}[z-\lambda_{i_{1}}(t)],\ldots,N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{\frac{1}{2}}[z-\lambda_{i_{k}}(t)])\right] \displaystyle-\int_{\mathbb{C}^{k}}O(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\rho_{\mathrm{univ},z,t}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})dz_{1}\ldots dz_{k} $$

vanishes as $N\to\infty$ , where $\{\lambda_{j}(t)\}_{j}$ are eigenvalues of $A+\sqrt{t}B$ , where

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{\mathrm{univ},z,t}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k}) \displaystyle=\Phi_{z,t}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})\rho_{\mathrm{GinUE}}^{(k)}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k}), $$

and where $\Phi_{z,t}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{k})$ is independent of the distribution of the entries of $A$ .

We give proofs of Theorems 1 and 2 in the case $k=2$ for (notational) convenience. For general $k\geq 2$ , the same argument with minor adjustments works; see [23] for details.

Now we discuss additional difficulties that arise in case of real non-symmetric i.i.d. ensembles in comparison with the complex case. In [23] the authors obtain the integral formula for the $k$ -point correlation function through a change of variables in the space of complex non-Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices $M_{N}(\mathbb{C})$ obtained by consecutive Householder transformations with respect to the eigenvectors. In our case, since real matrices still have complex eigenvalues, we have to adapt each step of the change of variable to isolate conjugate pairs of eigenvalues. This leads to another integration parameter $\theta$ , where $2\theta$ is the angle between the corresponding right eigenvectors. It turns out $\theta$ concentrates around the value $\pi/4$ . Showing this is one of the key steps, and the main challenge is that local law estimates do not seem to help; instead, we control the region $|\theta-\pi/4|\gg N^{-1/2+\delta}$ directly (here, $\delta>0$ is any small parameter). Additionally, to carry out the asymptotic analysis we need to show that certain resolvent quantities have universal deterministic approximations. In particular, we derive the local law and the two-resolvent local laws at scales proportional to $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ for the Hermitization of $I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda\otimes I_{N}$ , where $\Lambda$ is a deterministic $2\times 2$ matrix. This is a $2\times 2$ analogue of the $1\times 1$ results in [7, 3, 4, 9]. We prove this using the cumulant expansion argument commonly used for the proofs of two resolvent local laws, see [12, 8, 13, 1]. Our final step is to remove the Gaussian component $\sqrt{t}B$ , which amounts to a standard “three-and-a-half” moment comparison approach and the Girko formula as in [18, 10], respectively.

Finally, let us mention that approximately a week before posting to the arXiv, [26] was posted to the arXiv, in which the same result was proven by the same general strategy, but with different approaches to some of the technical challenges alluded to in the previous paragraph. (These technical differences potentially affect the smallest time-scale $t$ achievable.) It is possible that combining the methods of our paper with those of [26] may prove Theorem 2 for the optimal time-scale $t=N^{-1/2+\delta}$ . Osman [26] also proves bulk universality on the real line; for this, another method based on “spin variables” is employed to handle additional difficulties occuring therein. See [26] for details.

### 1.1 Notation

We use big-O notation, i.e. $a=O(b)$ means $|a|\leq C|b|$ for some constant $C>0$ . Any subscripts in the big-O notation indicate what parameters the constant $C$ depends on. We also write $a\lesssim b$ to mean $a=O(b)$ and $a\gtrsim b$ to mean $b=O(a)$ , with the same disclaimer about subscripts. We use the notation $[[a,b]]=[a,b]\cap{\mathbb{Z}}$ for an integer range.

## 2 Change-of-variables

The goal of this section is to reproduce ideas in [23] but for real non-symmetric matrices.

### 2.1 Preliminary steps

Define the manifolds

$$ \displaystyle\Omega \displaystyle:=\Omega_{1}\times\Omega_{2}\times M_{(N-4)\times(N-4)}(\mathbb{R}) \displaystyle\Omega_{1} \displaystyle:=\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}_{+}\times[0,\frac{\pi}{2})\times V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\times M_{(N-2)\times 2}(\mathbb{R}), \displaystyle\Omega_{2} \displaystyle:=\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}_{+}\times[0,\frac{\pi}{2})\times V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})\times M_{(N-4)\times 2}(\mathbb{R}). $$

Above, $V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is the Stiefel manifold

$$ \displaystyle V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}):=\mathbf{O}(d)/\mathbf{O}(d-2)=\{(v_{1},v_{2})\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}\times\mathbb{S}^{d-1}:v_{1}^{\ast}v_{2}=0\}, $$

where $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ is the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ . Define the map $\Phi:\Omega\to M_{N\times N}(\mathbb{R})$ given by

$$ \displaystyle\Phi(a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},W_{1},a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{w},W_{2},M^{(2)}) \displaystyle=R_{1}(\mathbf{v})\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}&W_{1}^{\ast}\\
0&M^{(1)}\end{pmatrix}R_{1}(\mathbf{v})^{\ast}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle M^{(1)}=R_{2}(\mathbf{u})\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}&W_{2}^{\ast}\\
0&M^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}R_{2}(\mathbf{u})^{\ast}. $$

Above, $R_{1}:V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})\to\mathbf{O}(N)$ is a smooth map such that for any $\mathbf{v}=(v_{1},v_{2})\in V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ , we have $R_{1}(\mathbf{v})\mathbf{e}_{i}=v_{i}$ for $i=1,2$ . Similarly, $R_{2}:V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})\to\mathbf{O}(N-2)$ is a smooth map such that for any $\mathbf{u}=(u_{1},u_{2})\in V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})$ , we have $R_{2}(\mathbf{u})\mathbf{e}_{i}=u_{i}$ for $i=1,2$ . Lastly, the matrix $\Lambda_{a,b,\theta}$ is given by

$$ \displaystyle\Lambda_{a,b,\theta}=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\tan\theta\\
-\frac{b}{\tan\theta}&a\end{pmatrix}. $$

Throughout, we will use the notation $\lambda_{j}=a_{j}+ib_{j}$ .

#### Lemma 3.

The Jacobian of the map $\Phi$ is given by

$$ \displaystyle J(\Phi) \displaystyle=\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}|\lambda_{1}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}|^{2} \displaystyle\times\left|\det\left(M^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}\right)\right|^{2}\left|\det\left(M^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}\right)\right|^{2}. $$

#### Proof.

See Appendix C. ∎

Define the following probability measure on $M_{N\times N}(\mathbb{R})$ , in which $A$ is a deterministic matrix:

$$ \displaystyle\rho(M)dM:=\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{N^{2}}{2}}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(M-A)^{\ast}(M-A)\right]\right\}dM. $$

By the change-of-variables formula and Lemma 3, we have

$$ \displaystyle\rho(M)dM=\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{N^{2}}{2}}\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}|\lambda_{1}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}|^{2} \displaystyle\times\left|\det\left(M^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}\right)\right|^{2}\left|\det\left(M^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}\right)\right|^{2}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(\Phi^{-1}M)^{\ast}(\Phi^{-1}M)\right\} \displaystyle\times da_{1}db_{1}d\theta_{1}d\mathbf{v}dW_{1}da_{2}db_{2}d\theta_{2}d\mathbf{u}dW_{2}dM^{(2)}, $$

where $\Phi^{-1}M$ is formal notation for the following matrix:

$$ \displaystyle\Phi^{-1}M \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta}&W_{1}^{\ast}\\
0&M^{(1)}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle M^{(1)} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}&W_{2}^{\ast}\\
0&M^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}. $$

We will integrate out all variables except $a_{1},b_{1},a_{2},b_{2}$ . In this subsection, we focus on integrating out just $W_{1},W_{2}$ , and $M^{(2)}$ .

Now, we write $A$ in terms of the basis induced by $R_{1}(\mathbf{v})$ and $R_{2}(\mathbf{u})$ . Precisely, we write

$$ \displaystyle A \displaystyle=R_{1}(\mathbf{v})\begin{pmatrix}A_{11}&B_{1}^{\ast}\\
C_{1}&A^{(1)}\end{pmatrix}R_{1}(\mathbf{v})^{\ast} \displaystyle A^{(1)} \displaystyle=R_{2}(\mathbf{u})\begin{pmatrix}A^{(1)}_{11}&B_{2}^{\ast}\\
C_{2}&A^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}R_{2}(\mathbf{u}). $$

We clarify that $A_{11}$ and $A^{(1)}_{11}$ are blocks of size $2\times 2$ . Finally, set $B^{(2)}:=M^{(2)}-A^{(2)}$ . An elementary computation shows that

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(\Phi^{-1}M)^{\ast}(\Phi^{-1}M) \displaystyle=\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2} \displaystyle+\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2} \displaystyle+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{1}-B_{1})^{\ast}(W_{1}-B_{1})\right] \displaystyle+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{2}-B_{2})^{\ast}(W_{2}-B_{2})\right] \displaystyle+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}. $$

From this, we get

$$ \displaystyle\rho(M)dM \displaystyle=\tilde{\rho}(a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},W_{1},a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u},W_{2},B^{(2)}) \displaystyle\times da_{1}db_{1}d\theta_{1}d\mathbf{v}dW_{1}da_{2}db_{2}d\theta_{2}d\mathbf{u}dW_{2}dB^{(2)}, $$

where $\tilde{\rho}(a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},W_{1},a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u},W_{2},B^{(2)})$ is given by

$$ \displaystyle\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{N^{2}}{2}}\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}|\lambda_{1}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}|^{2} \displaystyle\times\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}]\right|^{2}\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}]\right|^{2}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{1}-B_{1})^{\ast}(W_{1}-B_{1})\right]\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{2}-B_{2})^{\ast}(W_{2}-B_{2})\right]\right\}. $$

We note that $dM^{(2)}$ has turned into $dB^{(2)}$ ; the change-of-variable factor here is $1$ because the map $M^{(2)}\mapsto B^{(2)}$ is translation by $A^{(2)}$ . Also, we clarify that $B$ and $B_{1}$ are functions of all parameters except for $W_{1},W_{2}$ , respectively. Thus, by Gaussian integration, we have

$$ \displaystyle\int_{M_{(N-2)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{1}-B_{1})^{\ast}(W_{1}-B_{1})\right]\right\}dW_{1} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{2\pi t}{N}\right)^{N-2} \displaystyle\int_{M_{(N-4)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(W_{2}-B_{2})^{\ast}(W_{2}-B_{2})\right]\right\}dW_{2} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{2\pi t}{N}\right)^{N-4}. $$

So, by integrating out $W_{1},W_{2}$ , which appear only through the Gaussian weights in the last two lines, we get

$$ \displaystyle\int_{M_{(N-2)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})}\int_{M_{(N-4)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})}\tilde{\rho}(a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},W_{1},a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u},W_{2},B^{(2)})dW_{1}dW_{2} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{N^{2}-4N+12}{2}}\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}|\lambda_{1}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}|^{2} \displaystyle\times\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}]\right|^{2}\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}]\right|^{2}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2}\right\}. $$

We now integrate the previous expression over $B^{(2)}$ . First, let $M_{k}(\mathbb{R})$ be the space of $k\times k$ matrices with real entries.

#### Lemma 4.

We have the identity

$$ \displaystyle\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{N^{2}-4N+12}{2}}\int_{M_{N-4}(\mathbb{R})}\prod_{j=1,2}|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}]|^{2}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}}dB^{(2)} \displaystyle=2^{6}\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{2N+4}\int_{M^{skew}_{4}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX, $$

where $M_{4}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})$ is the space of $4\times 4$ skew-symmetric complex matrices, and

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}(X) \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}X\otimes I_{N-4}&A^{(2)}_{\mathbf{w}}\\
-\left(A^{(2)}_{\mathbf{w}}\right)^{T}&X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle A^{(2)}_{\mathbf{w}} \displaystyle:=\begin{bmatrix}I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4}&0\\
0&\left(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4}\right)^{\ast}\end{bmatrix} \displaystyle\mathbf{w} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{1}&0\\
0&\lambda_{2}\end{pmatrix}. $$

#### Proof.

This is very similar to the proof of Lemma 5.1 in [23]. We first use vectors $\chi_{1},\chi_{2},\psi_{1},\psi_{2}$ of anti-commuting Grassmann variables to write

$$ \displaystyle|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}]|^{2} \displaystyle=\int e^{-\chi_{j}^{\ast}(\lambda_{j}-A^{(2)}-B^{(2)})\chi_{j}-\psi_{j}^{\ast}(\overline{\lambda}_{j}-(A^{(2)})^{\ast}-(B^{(2)})^{\ast})\psi_{j}}d\chi_{j}d\psi_{j}. $$

From this, we get

$$ \displaystyle\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}]\right|^{2}\left|\det[A^{(2)}+B^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}]\right|^{2}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}} \displaystyle=\int\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}B^{(2)}\sum_{j=1,2}\chi_{j}\chi_{j}^{\ast}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}\sum_{j=1,2}\psi_{j}\psi_{j}^{\ast}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\sum_{j=1,2}\chi_{j}^{\ast}(\lambda_{j}-A^{(2)})\chi_{j}-\sum_{j=1,2}\psi_{j}^{\ast}(\overline{\lambda}_{j}-(A^{(2)})^{\ast})\psi_{j}\right\}d\chi_{1}d\chi_{2}d\psi_{1}d\psi_{2}. $$

We can integrate the first exponential factor over $B^{(2)}$ , since it is a Gaussian integral. We have

$$ \displaystyle\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{\frac{(N-4)^{2}}{2}}\int_{M_{N-4}(\mathbb{R})}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}B^{(2)}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}B^{(2)}\sum_{j=1,2}\chi_{j}\chi_{j}^{\ast}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}(B^{(2)})^{\ast}\sum_{j=1,2}\psi_{j}\psi_{j}^{\ast}}dB^{(2)} \displaystyle=\operatorname{exp}\left\{\frac{t}{2N}\sum_{k,m=1}^{N-4}\left(\sum_{j=1,2}\left(\chi_{j,k}\bar{\chi}_{j,m}+\psi_{j,m}\bar{\psi}_{j,k}\right)\right)^{2}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{t}{N}\sum_{j,\ell=1,2}(\chi_{j}^{\ast}\psi_{\ell})(\psi_{\ell}^{\ast}\chi_{j})-\frac{t}{N}(\chi_{1}^{T}\chi_{2})(\chi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\chi}_{1})-\frac{t}{N}(\psi_{1}^{T}\psi_{2})(\psi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\psi}_{1})\right\}, $$

where the last identity follows by anti-commuting of Grassmann variables. By Gaussian integration, we can again write

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{t}{N}\sum_{j,\ell=1,2}(\chi_{j}^{\ast}\psi_{\ell})(\psi_{\ell}^{\ast}\chi_{j})\right\} \displaystyle=\left(\frac{N}{\pi t}\right)^{4}\int_{M_{2}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}Y-i\sum_{j,\ell=1,2}(Y_{j\ell}\chi_{j}^{\ast}\psi_{\ell}+\overline{Y}_{j\ell}\psi_{\ell}^{\ast}\chi_{j})}dY \displaystyle=2^{4}\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{4}\int_{M_{2}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}Y-i\sum_{j,\ell=1,2}(Y_{j\ell}\chi_{j}^{\ast}\psi_{\ell}+\overline{Y}_{j\ell}\psi_{\ell}^{\ast}\chi_{j})}dY. $$

and, similarly,

$$ \displaystyle\frac{t}{N}(\chi_{1}^{T}\chi_{2})(\chi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\chi}_{1})=2\frac{N}{2\pi t}\int_{\mathbb{C}}e^{-\frac{N}{t}|S|^{2}-i\bar{S}\chi_{1}^{T}\chi_{2}-iS\chi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\chi}_{1}}dS \displaystyle\frac{t}{N}(\psi_{1}^{T}\psi_{2})(\psi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\psi}_{1})=2\frac{N}{2\pi t}\int_{\mathbb{C}}e^{-\frac{N}{t}|T|^{2}-i\bar{T}\psi_{1}^{T}\psi_{2}-iT\psi_{2}^{\ast}\bar{\psi}_{1}}dT. $$

Now we change the integration variables from $Y,S,T$ to $X\in M^{skew}_{4}(\mathbb{C})$ defined by

$$ X=\begin{pmatrix}\begin{matrix}0&iS\\
-iS&0\end{matrix}&iY\\
-iY^{T}&\begin{matrix}0&iT\\
-iT&0\end{matrix}\end{pmatrix}. $$

The Jacobian of this change of variables is $1$ . Since all remaining terms involving Grassmann variables are now quadratic in $\chi$ , $\psi$ , we can combine them into an exponent of a quadratic form and integrate

$$ \int e^{-\frac{1}{2}\phi^{T}\mathbf{M}(X)\phi}d\phi=\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)], $$

where $\phi^{T}=(\chi_{1}^{\ast},\chi_{2}^{\ast},\psi_{1}^{T},\psi_{2}^{T},\chi_{1}^{T},\chi_{2}^{T},-\psi_{1}^{\ast},-\psi_{2}^{\ast})$ and $\mathbf{M}(X)$ is defined in the statement of the lemma. It remains to collect the Gaussian weights

$$ \operatorname{exp}\left\{-\frac{N}{t}\left({\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}Y+|S|^{2}+|T|^{2}\right)\right\}=\operatorname{exp}\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X\right\} $$

and the proof is finished. ∎

### 2.2 Re-parameterizing $\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{2}$

By Lemma 4, we have

$$ \displaystyle\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}M_{(N-2)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})\\
M_{(N-2)\times 2}(\mathbb{R})\\
M_{(N-2)\times(N-2)}(\mathbb{R})\end{subarray}}\tilde{\rho}(a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},W_{1},a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u},W_{2},B^{(2)})dW_{1}dW_{2}dB^{(2)} \displaystyle=2^{6}\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{2N+4}\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}|\lambda_{1}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}|\lambda_{1}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}|^{2} \displaystyle\times\int_{M^{skew}_{4}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{2},b_{2},\theta_{2}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle=:\tilde{\rho}(\lambda_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},\lambda_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u}). $$

Recall $\lambda_{j}=a_{j}+ib_{j}$ . We now re-parameterize $\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}$ as to be in a neighborhood of a fixed point $z=a+ib\in\mathbb{C}$ of radius $\sqrt{N}$ ; we emphasize that we always assume $b>0$ . Set $\mathbf{z}=(z_{1},z_{2})$ and define

$$ \displaystyle\rho_{t}(z,\mathbf{z};A) \displaystyle:=\frac{1}{N^{2}\sigma_{z,t}^{2}}\tilde{\rho}\left(z+\frac{z_{1}}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}},z+\frac{z_{2}}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}\right), \displaystyle\tilde{\rho}(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}) \displaystyle:=\int_{[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]}\int_{[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})}\tilde{\rho}(\lambda_{1},\theta_{1},\mathbf{v},\lambda_{2},\theta_{2},\mathbf{u})d\theta_{1}d\theta_{2}d\mathbf{v}d\mathbf{u}. $$

Here $d\mathbf{u}$ and $d\mathbf{v}$ are defined as integration with respect to the rotationally invariant volume form on $V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ and $V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})$ , respectively. In view of the previous definitions, we will also always identify $\lambda_{j}=z+N^{-1/2}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1/2}z_{j}$ for $j=1,2$ . We now follow [23] and define

$$ \displaystyle\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)}) \displaystyle:=\frac{4N}{\pi^{4}t^{4}\sigma_{z,t}^{3}}|z_{1}-z_{2}|^{2}{|z-\overline{z}|^{2}}\int_{M^{skew}_{4}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX \displaystyle\tilde{K}_{1}(z_{1}) \displaystyle:=\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{N}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2}\right\}d\mathbf{v} \displaystyle\tilde{K}_{2}(z_{2}) \displaystyle:=\left(\frac{N}{2\pi t}\right)^{N}\int_{V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2}\right\}d\mathbf{u} \displaystyle d\nu_{1}(\mathbf{v}) \displaystyle:=\tilde{K}_{1}(z_{1})^{-1}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N}\right]\mathbf{v}\right\|^{2}\right\}d\mathbf{v}, \displaystyle d\nu_{2}(\mathbf{u}) \displaystyle:=\tilde{K}_{2}(z_{2})^{-1}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}\left\|\left[I_{2}\otimes A^{(1)}-\Lambda_{a_{1},b_{1},\theta_{1}}\otimes I_{N-2}\right]\mathbf{u}\right\|^{2}\right\}d\mathbf{u}. $$

The scaling above is chosen because the $V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ and $V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N-2})$ integration resemble Gaussian integration with variance $N^{-1}$ ; this is why we want $N^{N}$ factors with $\tilde{K}_{j}(z_{j})$ terms. Finite powers of $N$ , on the other hand, will not be important to keep track of carefully (since all error terms will be either come from multiplicative factors $1+o(1)$ or be exponentially small in $N$ ).

Again, by identifying $\lambda_{j}=z+N^{-1/2}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1/2}z_{j}$ , in the formula (2.2) for the matrix $\mathbf{M}(X)$ , we can write

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{w}=\begin{pmatrix}z+\frac{z_{1}}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}&0\\
0&z+\frac{z_{2}}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}\end{pmatrix}. $$

With this notation, we can write

$$ \displaystyle\rho(z;\mathbf{z},A):= \displaystyle\int_{[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]^{2}}\frac{256b_{1}^{2}b_{2}^{2}|\cos 2\theta_{1}||\cos 2\theta_{2}|}{|\sin^{2}2\theta_{1}|\sin^{2}2\theta_{2}|}\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)})\tilde{K}_{1}(z_{1})\tilde{K}_{2}(z_{2})d\nu_{1}(\mathbf{v})d\nu_{2}(\mathbf{u})d\theta_{1}d\theta_{2} \displaystyle\times\left[1+O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}}))\right]. $$

We will estimate $\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)})$ following the ideas in [23]. We will then give a preliminary Fourier transform computation for $\tilde{K}_{j}(z_{j})$ . Ultimately, the main problem for real non-symmetric matrices is the integration over $\theta$ , which we explain further and start dealing with in the next section.

### 2.3 Estimating $\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)})$

The goal of this subsection is to prove the following analog of Lemma 4.1 in [23]. Before we state this lemma, we first introduce the following notation (in which $j\in\{1,2\}$ ):

$$ \displaystyle Z_{j} \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}0&z_{j}\\
\overline{z}_{j}&0\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle\delta_{z,t} \displaystyle=\langle[H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})(A-z)]^{2}\rangle, \displaystyle\tau_{z,t} \displaystyle=\frac{\gamma_{z,t}\delta_{z,t}-\beta^{2}_{z,t}}{\gamma_{z,t}\sigma_{z,t}}, \displaystyle\psi_{j} \displaystyle:=\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}]-\mathrm{Re}(\overline{\tau}_{z,t}z_{j}^{2})+|z_{j}|^{2}\right\} \displaystyle V_{1} \displaystyle:=V_{1}(\mathbf{v}):=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{v}_{1}&\mathbf{v}_{2}&0&0\\
0&0&\mathbf{v}_{1}&\mathbf{v}_{2}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle V_{2} \displaystyle:=V_{2}(\mathbf{u}):=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{u}_{1}&\mathbf{u}_{2}&0&0\\
0&0&\mathbf{u}_{1}&\mathbf{u}_{2}\end{pmatrix} $$

We clarify that the dimension of $V_{1}$ is $2N\times 4$ and the dimension of $V_{2}$ is $2(N-2)\times 4$ . Also, for the rest of this paper, when we say “locally uniformly in $a_{j},b_{j}$ ”, we mean for $a_{j},b_{j}=O(1)$ , so that the eigenvalues are $\lambda_{j}=z+O(N^{-1/2})$ uniformly in $N$ . (We will also use “locally uniformly in $z_{j}$ ” to mean the same thing.) Next, let us introduce the constant

$$ \displaystyle\upsilon_{z,t}:= \displaystyle\pi\left[Nt^{-1}-N\langle(A-z)^{\ast}\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{z}}(\eta_{z,t})(A-z)\rangle\right] \displaystyle\times\left[Nt^{-1}-N\langle(A-z)H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})H_{\overline{z}}(\eta_{z,t})(A-\overline{z})\rangle\right]. $$

Lastly, we emphasize that all estimates hold with high probability with respect to randomness of $A$ , i.e. with probability at least $1-o(1)$ . We only need a finite number of estimates, so the end result holds with high probability (i.e. on an event which contributes $o(1)$ in the expectations in Theorems 1 and 2). To avoid being verbose, we will not always explicitly mention this, e.g. when it concerns local law estimates in Lemmas 26 and 29.

#### Lemma 5.

We have the following locally uniformly in $z_{1},z_{2}$ , where $\kappa>0$ :

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)})}{\rho_{\mathrm{GinUE}}^{(2)}(z_{1},z_{2})} \displaystyle=\frac{32\pi^{3}{|z-\overline{z}|^{2}}}{Nt^{4}\gamma_{z,t}^{2}\sigma_{z,t}^{3}\upsilon_{z,t}^{2}}e^{-\frac{2N}{t}\eta_{z,t}^{2}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,2}|\det[V_{j}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(j-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{j}]|^{2}\psi_{j}\left[1+O(N^{-\kappa})\right]. $$

#### Proof.

Before we begin, let us first comment on the strategy. The argument amounts to removing the diagonal $2\times 2$ blocks from generic $X\in M_{4}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})$ in the integration in $\tilde{F}(\mathbf{z};A^{(2)})$ . Indeed, in view of the proof of Lemma 4, these diagonal blocks correspond to extra terms which differentiate the real case from the complex case as in Section 5 of [23]. After this, we are left with a very similar computation as in Section 5 of [23]. (In fact, bulk correlation functions should agree between real and complex matrix ensembles for eigenvalues away from the real line, so we must arrive at the same Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber integral as in the complex case of [23].)

For any $X\in M_{4}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})$ , set $P=XX^{\ast}$ and $Q=X^{\ast}X$ . For $\delta>0$ small but fixed, write

$$ \displaystyle\int_{M_{4}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX \displaystyle=\int_{\|P-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\mathrm{max}}\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX+\Upsilon \displaystyle=:\Upsilon_{0}+\Upsilon, $$

where $\|\|_{\max}$ is the max-entry norm, and $\Upsilon$ is an error term that satisfies the bound

$$ \displaystyle|\Upsilon| \displaystyle\leq\sum_{j=1,\ldots,4}\int_{|P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\geq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}dX \displaystyle+\sum_{j=1,\ldots,4}\int_{|Q_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\geq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}dX \displaystyle+\sum_{j,\ell,k=1,\ldots,4}\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}|P_{j\ell}|,|Q_{j\ell}|\geq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\\
|P_{kk}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\\
|Q_{kk}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\end{subarray}}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}dX \displaystyle=:\Upsilon_{1}+\Upsilon_{2}+\Upsilon_{3}. $$

(We have used the fact that since $X$ is size $O(1)$ , we know $\|P-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}=O(N^{\delta-1/2})$ is equivalent to $\|Q-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}=O(N^{\delta-1/2})$ . We also used $|\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}]|\leq|\det[\mathbf{M}]|^{1/2}$ for a skew symmetric matrix $\mathbf{M}$ .) We first bound $\Upsilon$ . We treat the region $|P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\geq N^{\delta-1/2}$ for $j=1,\ldots,4$ . We claim

$$ \displaystyle|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]| \displaystyle=|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\leq\det[P\otimes I_{N-4}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}(A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)})^{\ast}]^{\frac{1}{2}}\det[Q\otimes I_{N-4}+(A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)})^{\ast}A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}]^{\frac{1}{2}}. $$

The second line follows by computing explicitly the diagonal entries of $\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}$ and then using Lemma 2.2 in [23] (Fisher’s inequality) to bound $|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}]|$ by the product of determinants of its diagonal blocks. If we again compute each matrix in the second line and apply Lemma 2.2 in [23], we obtain

$$ \displaystyle|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\leq\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}|\det[P_{jj}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}|^{2}]|^{\frac{1}{4}}|\det[Q_{jj}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}|^{2}]|^{\frac{1}{4}}, $$

where $\lambda_{3}=\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{4}=\lambda_{2}$ . Multiply and divide by $\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]$ . This gives

$$ \displaystyle|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\leq\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,2}\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}\left\{\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+P_{jj}]}{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\right\}^{\frac{1}{4}} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}\left\{\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+Q_{jj}]}{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\right\}^{\frac{1}{4}}. $$

Let us control the first product, i.e. the ratio of determinants. We first have

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]} \displaystyle=\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\frac{\det[(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]} \displaystyle=\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\frac{\det\begin{pmatrix}i\eta_{z,t}&A-\lambda_{j}\\
(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}&i\eta_{z,t}\end{pmatrix}}{\det\begin{pmatrix}i\eta_{z,t}&A-z\\
(A-z)^{\ast}&i\eta_{z,t}\end{pmatrix}} \displaystyle=\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\det\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right]. $$

We now rewrite the last determinant as exponential of trace of log, after which we expand the logarithm to get

$$ \displaystyle\det\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right] \displaystyle=\exp\left\{{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right]\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k(N\sigma_{z,t})^{\frac{k}{2}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[\left(G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right)^{k}\right]\right\}. $$

We can bound the $k\geq 3$ contribution by using the trivial operator norm bound $\|G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-1}\lesssim t^{-1}$ . Using also uniform boundedness of $\sigma_{z,t}$ away from $0$ , this gives (for some $C=O(1)$ )

$$ \displaystyle\left|\sum_{k=3}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k(N\sigma_{z,t})^{\frac{k}{2}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j})^{k}\right]\right|\lesssim\sum_{k=3}^{\infty}C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}+1}t^{-\frac{k}{2}}\lesssim N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-\frac{3}{2}} $$

assuming $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ with $\epsilon_{0}>0$ small. Let us now separate the $k=1,2$ terms:

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{2\sigma_{z,t}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle\right\}. $$

A straightforward computation using (1.1) and $(A-z)^{\ast}\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta)=H_{z}(\eta)(A-z)$ shows that

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2\sigma_{z,t}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle \displaystyle=\frac{1}{\sigma_{z,t}}\eta_{z,t}^{2}|z_{j}|^{2}\langle H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\rangle \displaystyle-\frac{z_{j}^{2}\langle[(A-z)^{\ast}H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}\rangle}{2\sigma_{z,t}} \displaystyle-\frac{\overline{z}_{j}^{2}\langle[H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})(A-z)]^{2}\rangle}{2\sigma_{z,t}}. $$

By definition of $\sigma_{z,t}$ , we know that the first term on the RHS is equal to $|z_{j}|^{2}-\beta_{z,t}^{2}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}\gamma_{z,t}^{-1}|z_{j}|^{2}$ . Next, note $\langle[H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})(A-z)]^{2}\rangle=\overline{\langle(A-z)^{\ast}H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}\rangle}$ since $H_{z}(\eta_{z,t})$ is self-adjoint. So, the second and third terms on the RHS of the previous identity combine to $-\mathrm{Re}(\overline{\delta_{z,t}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}z_{j}^{2})=-\mathrm{Re}(\overline{\tau_{z,t}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}z_{j}^{2})+\beta_{z,t}^{2}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}\gamma_{z,t}^{-1}\mathrm{Re}(z_{j}^{2})$ . Thus, in total, the previous display is $\leq|z_{j}|^{2}-\mathrm{Re}(\overline{\tau_{z,t}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}z_{j}^{2})$ , and

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{2\sigma_{z,t}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle\right\} \displaystyle\leq\exp\left\{-N^{\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}\langle G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\rangle-\mathrm{Re}(\overline{\tau}_{z,t}\sigma_{z,t}^{-1}z_{j}^{2})+|z_{j}|^{2}\right\}=\psi_{j}. $$

Thus, we have

$$ \displaystyle\det\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right] \displaystyle=\psi_{j}\exp\left\{-\sum_{k=3}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k(N\sigma_{z,t})^{\frac{k}{2}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[\left(G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}\right)^{k}\right]\right\} \displaystyle=\psi_{j}\left[1+O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-3})\right]. $$

We now compute the remaining ratio of determinants using Cramer’s rule to replace $A^{(2)}$ by $A^{(1)}$ and then by $A$ . This is the same procedure as in (5.7) of [23], but now the subspaces that we project resolvents onto must be spanned by pairs $\mathbf{v}\in V^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{N})$ . Specifically, this gives

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}{\det[(A-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]} \displaystyle=\prod_{\ell=1,2}\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|, $$

where $G_{w}^{(\ell)}(\eta)$ is the same as $G_{w}(\eta)$ but replacing $A$ by $A^{(\ell)}$ . We now replace $G^{(\ell-1)}_{\lambda_{j}}$ by $G^{(\ell-1)}_{z}$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right| \displaystyle=\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|\frac{\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|}{\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|} $$

and, by the resolvent identity, we also have the following (in which $G_{w}=G_{w}(\eta_{z,t})$ for convenience):

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|}{\left|\det\left[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}\right]\right|} \displaystyle=\left|\det\left[1+(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}(G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell)}-G_{z}^{(\ell-1)})V_{\ell}^{\ast}\right]\right| \displaystyle=\left|\det\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}\right]\right|. $$

To control this determinant we are left with, we will again write it as exponential of a trace of a log and then expand the log. To this end, we need the following estimate, which uses only Lemma 2.1 of [23] and some elementary manipulations:

$$ \displaystyle N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left|{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}\right]^{k}\right| \displaystyle=N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left|{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}\right]^{k}\right| \displaystyle\lesssim N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left\|G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k} \displaystyle\lesssim C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left\|G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k} \displaystyle\leq C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left\|G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k}\|[G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}]^{-1}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k} \displaystyle\lesssim C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left\|[\mathrm{Im}(G_{z}^{(\ell-1)})^{-1}]^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k}\|[G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}]^{-1}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k} \displaystyle=C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left\|[\mathrm{Im}(G_{z}^{(\ell-1)})^{-1}]^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k}\left\|I+N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}Z_{j}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k} \displaystyle=C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-k}(1+O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-1})). $$

We clarify that the operator norm bound for the trace follows because the matrix in question rank $O(1)$ . Since $\eta_{z,t}\gg N^{-1/2}$ , the big-O term in the last line is $\ll 1$ . Thus, we have

$$ \displaystyle\left|\det\left[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{N\sigma_{z,t}}}(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}\right]\right| \displaystyle\leq\exp\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{k}{2}}\left|{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[(V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell})^{-1}V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}Z_{j}G_{\lambda_{j}}^{(\ell-1)}V_{\ell}\right]^{k}\right|\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}O(C^{k}N^{-\frac{k}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-k})\right\}=1+O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-1}). $$

Gathering all of this, we deduce

$$ \displaystyle|\det[\mathbf{M}(X)]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\lesssim\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}\left\{\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+P_{jj}]}{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\right\}^{\frac{1}{4}} \displaystyle\times\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}\left\{\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+Q_{jj}]}{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]}\right\}^{\frac{1}{4}}. $$

It remains to control the last two products over $j$ ; we treat the first, since the second is handled in the same way. By resolvent perturbation and the inequality $\log(1+x)\leq x-\frac{3x^{2}}{6+4x}$ , we have the following, for which we use the notation $\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}):=A_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2),\ast}A_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}+\eta_{z,t}^{2}$

$$ \displaystyle\frac{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+P_{jj}]}{\det[(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j})+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]} \displaystyle=\det\left[I_{N-4}+(P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2})\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\right] \displaystyle=\exp\left\{{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\log\left[I_{N-4}+(P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2})\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\right]\right\} \displaystyle\leq\exp\left\{(P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})-\frac{3(P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2})}{6+4\frac{|P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}|}{\eta_{z,t}^{2}}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}\right\}. $$

By combining the previous two displays and by $\frac{t}{N}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})=1$ , we have the following parallel to (5.6) in [23]:

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{1} \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-\frac{2N\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{t}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2} \displaystyle\times\sum_{k=1,\ldots,4}\int_{|P_{kk}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}}\exp\left\{-\frac{Nt}{4}\sum_{j=1,\ldots,4}h_{j}(\eta_{z,t}^{-2}|p_{j}|)-\frac{Nt}{4}\sum_{j=1,\ldots,4}h_{j}(\eta_{z,t}^{-2}|q_{j}|)\right\}dX, $$

where $p_{j}=P_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}$ and $q_{j}=Q_{jj}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}$ and

$$ \displaystyle h_{j}(x):=\frac{\eta_{z,t}^{4}}{Nt}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}\frac{3x^{2}}{6+4x}-\frac{\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{Nt}\left({\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})]-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})]\right)x. $$

By interlacing of eigenvalues and the bound $\|\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\eta_{z,t}^{-2}$ , we replace $N^{-1}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}$ by $N^{-1}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}+O(N^{-1}\eta_{z,t}^{-4})$ . By the same token, we can also replace $N^{-1}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})]$ by $N^{-1}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})]+O(N^{-1}\eta_{z,t}^{-2})$ . We can then use a resolvent perturbation to show

$$ \displaystyle{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})]-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})] \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2N\eta_{z,t}}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\mathrm{Im}(G_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})-G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})) \displaystyle=\frac{1}{2N\eta_{z,t}}\mathrm{Im}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\left[N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{z,t}^{-\frac{1}{2}}G_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})Z_{j}G_{z}(\eta_{z,t})\right] \displaystyle=O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}}\eta_{z,t}^{-3}). $$

Lastly, we have the lower bound $N^{-1}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\tilde{H}_{\lambda{j}}(\eta_{z,t})]^{2}\geq C>0$ , since $\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}(\eta_{z,t})$ is the resolvent of a bounded operator. So, we obtain the lower bound $h_{j}(x)\geq C\eta_{z,t}^{3}(\frac{x^{2}}{1+x}-\frac{1}{N\eta_{z,t}^{3}}x)\geq C\eta_{z,t}^{3}\frac{x^{2}}{1+x}$ because $\eta=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ with $\epsilon_{0}>0$ small. (The discrepancy in the powers of $\eta_{z,t}$ compared to [23] will not be important; they come from using trivial bounds for resolvents as opposed to local law estimates.) In particular, if we take $\epsilon_{0}>0$ small enough in $\eta_{z,t}=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ , then as in [23], the integration over $|P_{kk}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}|\geq N^{-1/2+\delta}$ is exponentially small, i.e. for some $\kappa>0$ , we have

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{1}\lesssim e^{-CN^{\kappa}}e^{-\frac{2N\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{t}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2}. $$

By reversing the roles of $X$ and $X^{\ast}$ , the same argument implies

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{2}\lesssim e^{-CN^{\kappa}}e^{-\frac{2N\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{t}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2}. $$

So, we are left to bound $\Upsilon_{3}$ ; let us treat the case $(j,\ell)=(1,2)$ , since the other terms in $\Upsilon_{3}$ are treated in the same way. For this, we again start with (2.20). Now, let $P_{1}$ denote the upper left $2\times 2$ block of $P=XX^{\ast}$ . We now use Fisher’s inequality (Lemma 2.2 in [23]) again, but now with the top left $2\times 2$ block, the $(3,3)$ entry, and the $(4,4)$ entry as our diagonal blocks. This gives

$$ \displaystyle\det[P\otimes I_{N-4}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}(A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)})^{\ast}] \displaystyle\leq|\det[P_{1}\otimes I_{N-4}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4})(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}]| \displaystyle\times|\det[P_{33}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})^{\ast}]\det[P_{44}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2})(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2})^{\ast}]. $$

We now use the Schur complement formula to get the first line below, after which we factor out $P_{22}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}$ from the second determinant:

$$ \displaystyle\det[P_{1}\otimes I_{N-4}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4})(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}] \displaystyle=\det[P_{11}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}]\det[P_{22}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}-P_{12}(P_{11}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}|^{2})^{-1}P_{12}] \displaystyle=\det\left[1-|P_{12}|^{2}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{11})H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{22})\right]\det[P_{11}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}]\det[P_{22}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}]. $$

(Recall $H_{w}^{(2)}(\eta)=[(A-w)(A-w)^{\ast}+\eta^{2}]^{-1}$ .) Now, we use the inequality $\det(I+B)\leq e^{{\operatorname{Tr}\,}B}$ and the lower bounds $H^{(2)}_{\lambda_{j}}(P_{11}),H^{(2)}_{\lambda_{j}}(P_{22})\geq C>0$ (since they are resolvents of covariance matrices with bounded operator norm) to get

$$ \displaystyle\det\left[1-|P_{12}|^{2}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{11})H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{22})\right] \displaystyle\leq\exp\left\{-|P_{12}|^{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{11})H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{22})\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-|P_{12}|^{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{22})]^{\frac{1}{2}}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{11})[H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(P_{22})]^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\} \displaystyle\leq\exp\{-CN|P_{12}|^{2}\}. $$

A similar bound holds for $Q$ in place of $P$ . Let us clarify that the effect of using Fisher’s inequality with one $2\times 2$ matrix is to produce the determinant factor in (2.33), which produces an a priori exponential bound on the off-diagonal entry of said $2\times 2$ matrix. We shortly apply this principle again. We can now follow our computations for the bounds on $\Upsilon_{1}$ and $\Upsilon_{2}$ ; the only difference is the presence of $\exp\{-CN|P_{12}|^{2}\}$ and $\exp\{-CN|Q_{12}|^{2}\}$ . But we restrict to the set $|P_{12}|,|Q_{12}|\geq N^{\delta-1/2}$ . Ultimately, we deduce

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{3} \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-CN^{\kappa}}e^{-\frac{2N\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{t}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2}. $$

We are left with $\Upsilon_{0}$ . We must compute $\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}$ more precisely as follows:

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}=\begin{pmatrix}X\otimes I_{N-4}&A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}\\
(-A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)})^{T}&X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}&-A^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}\\
(A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)})^{\ast}&X\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}XX^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}[A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}&-X\otimes I_{N-4}A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}X\otimes I_{N-4}\\
-[A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}+X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}[A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}&X^{\ast}X\otimes I_{N-4}+[A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}\end{pmatrix}. $$

In particular, we must compute the off-diagonal blocks. Note that the bottom left block is the adjoint of the upper right block (indeed, $\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}$ must be Hermitian). So, we compute the top right block. First, since $X\in M_{4}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})$ , we can write

$$ \displaystyle X \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}X^{1}&Y\\
-Y^{T}&X^{2}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}X^{1}_{11}&X^{1}_{12}&Y_{11}&Y_{12}\\
-X^{1}_{12}&X^{1}_{22}&Y_{21}&Y_{22}\\
-Y_{11}&-Y_{21}&X^{2}_{11}&X^{2}_{12}\\
-Y_{12}&-Y^{22}&-X^{2}_{12}&X^{2}_{22}\end{pmatrix} $$

where $X^{1},X^{2}\in M_{2}^{skew}(\mathbb{C})$ and $Y\in M_{2\times 2}(\mathbb{C})$ . By definition, $A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}X\otimes I_{N-4}$ is equal to

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}&0&0&0\\
0&A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}&0&0\\
0&0&A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{1}&0\\
0&0&0&A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}X^{1}_{11}&X^{1}_{12}&Y_{11}&Y_{12}\\
-X^{1}_{12}&X^{1}_{22}&Y_{21}&Y_{22}\\
-Y_{11}&-Y_{21}&X^{2}_{11}&X^{2}_{12}\\
-Y_{12}&-Y^{22}&-X^{2}_{12}&X^{2}_{22}\end{pmatrix}. $$

The top left $2\times 2$ block of this $4\times 4$ matrix is given by

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}X_{11}^{1}[A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}]&X^{1}_{12}[A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}]\\
-X_{12}^{1}[A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}]&X^{1}_{22}[A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}]\end{pmatrix}. $$

We can compute $X\otimes I_{N-4}A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}$ in the exact same way. Its top left $2\times 2$ block is equal to

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}X_{11}^{1}[A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{1}]&X^{1}_{12}[A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}]\\
-X_{12}^{1}[A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{1}]&X^{1}_{22}[A^{(2)}-\overline{\lambda}_{2}]\end{pmatrix}. $$

Thus, the top left $2\times 2$ block of $-X\otimes I_{N-4}A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}X\otimes I_{N-4}$ is equal to

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}X^{1}_{11}[\overline{\lambda}_{1}-\lambda_{1}]&X^{1}_{12}[\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}]\\
-X^{1}_{12}[\overline{\lambda}_{1}-\lambda_{2}]&X^{1}_{22}[\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{2}]\end{pmatrix}. $$

The top left $2\times 2$ block of $-[A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}+X^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}[A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}$ is just the adjoint of the previous display, as we mentioned earlier. Now, return to (2.35). We apply Fisher’s inequality (Lemma 2.2 in [23]) once again with the following choices for blocks. First, we choose the $2\times 2$ block made up of the $(1,1)$ entry of $XX^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}+A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}[A_{\mathbf{w}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}$ , the $(2,2)$ entry of $X^{\ast}X\otimes I_{N-4}+[A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}]^{\ast}A_{\overline{\mathbf{w}}}^{(2)}$ , the $(1,2)$ entry of (2.36), and the $(2,1)$ entry of its adjoint (in the bottom left block of the second line of (2.35)). Precisely, this block is

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}P_{11}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})^{\ast}&X_{12}^{1}[\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}]\\
\overline{X}_{12}[\lambda_{2}-\overline{\lambda}_{1}]&Q_{22}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})\end{pmatrix}. $$

This picks out a $2\times 2$ diagonal block in (2.35). Note that its determinant is given by

$$ \displaystyle\det\begin{pmatrix}P_{11}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})^{\ast}&X_{12}^{1}[\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}]\\
\overline{X}_{12}[\lambda_{2}-\overline{\lambda}_{1}]&Q_{22}+(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})^{\ast}(A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1})\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle=\det[P_{11}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}]\det[Q_{22}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{2}|^{2}]\det[1-|X_{12}^{1}|^{2}|\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\sqrt{P_{11}})\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\sqrt{Q_{22}})]. $$

For applying Fisher’s inequality, we now take the $1\times 1$ blocks given by the remaining diagonal entries of the second line in (2.35). We get the following (in which $|L|^{2}=LL^{\ast}$ ):

$$ \displaystyle\det[\mathbf{M}(X)\mathbf{M}(X)^{\ast}] \displaystyle\leq\prod_{j=1,\ldots,4}|\det[P_{jj}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}|^{2}]||\det[Q_{jj}+|A^{(2)}-\lambda_{j}|^{2}]| \displaystyle\times\det[1-|X_{12}^{1}|^{2}|\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}H_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\sqrt{P_{11}})\tilde{H}_{\lambda_{j}}^{(2)}(\sqrt{Q_{22}})]. $$

Now, because $P_{11},Q_{11}=O(1)$ by our cutoff in the integration domain of $\Upsilon_{0}$ , as in (2.33), we know that the second line of the previous display is $\leq\exp[-CN|X_{12}^{1}|^{2}|\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}]$ ; this follows by the same argument as in (2.33). But $\lambda_{j}=z+O(N^{-1/2})$ locally uniformly in $a_{j},b_{j}$ , and $z\not\in\mathbb{R}$ is fixed, so $|\overline{\lambda}_{2}-\lambda_{1}|^{2}\gtrsim 1$ locally uniformly in $a_{j},b_{j}$ , and thus the second line of the previous display is $\leq\exp[-CN|X_{12}^{1}|^{2}]$ locally uniformly in $a_{j},b_{j}$ . We can now proceed as in our bound on $\Upsilon_{3}$ to restrict further the integration domain in $\Upsilon_{0}$ to the set where $|X_{12}|\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ for any small $\delta>0$ . We can do the same for every other entry of $X^{1}$ and every entry of $X^{2}$ as well. Ultimately, we have

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{0}=\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}}+\Upsilon_{4}, $$

where for some $\kappa>0$ small but fixed, we have

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}} \displaystyle:=\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}\|P-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\mathrm{max}}\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\\
\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\end{subarray}}e^{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{\ast}X}\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]dX, \displaystyle|\Upsilon_{4}| \displaystyle\lesssim e^{-CN^{\kappa}}e^{-\frac{2N\eta_{z,t}^{2}}{t}}\det[(A-z)^{\ast}(A-z)+\eta_{z,t}^{2}]^{2}\psi_{1}\psi_{2}\prod_{\ell=1,2}|\det[V_{\ell}^{\ast}G_{z}^{(\ell-1)}(\eta_{z,t})V_{\ell}]|^{2}. $$

In view of the cutoff of $\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}}$ , we now decompose $\mathbf{M}(X)$ as

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}(X) \displaystyle=\tilde{\mathbf{M}}(Y)+\tilde{\mathbf{M}}(X^{1},X^{2}), $$

where $\tilde{\mathbf{M}}(X^{1},X^{2})$ is a diagonal $4\times 4$ block matrix with diagonal entries $X^{1}\otimes I_{N-4},X^{2}\otimes I_{N-4},X^{1,\ast}\otimes I_{N-4},X^{2,\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}$ , and where $\tilde{\mathbf{M}}(Y)$ is the following block matrix:

$$ \displaystyle\begin{pmatrix}0&Y\otimes I_{N-4}&I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4}&0\\
-Y^{T}\otimes I_{N-4}&0&0&I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\overline{\mathbf{w}}\otimes I_{N-4}\\
-I_{2}\otimes A^{(2),\ast}+\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4}&0&0&-\overline{Y}\otimes I_{N-4}\\
0&-I_{2}\otimes A^{(2),\ast}+\overline{\mathbf{w}}\otimes I_{N-4}&Y^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}&0\end{pmatrix} $$

Because we take Pfaffian, We can change basis by sending $\mathbf{e}_{1}\mapsto\mathbf{e}_{1},\mathbf{e}_{3}\mapsto\mathbf{e}_{2},\mathbf{e}_{4}\mapsto\mathbf{e}_{3},\mathbf{e}_{2}\mapsto\mathbf{e}_{4}$ . In this new basis, we then have

$$ \displaystyle|\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(X)]| \displaystyle=|\operatorname{Pf}[\mathbf{M}(Y)+\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]|=|\det[\mathbf{M}(Y)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}|\det[1+\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]|^{\frac{1}{2}}, $$

where

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2}) \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}X^{1}\otimes I_{N-4}&0&0&0\\
0&X^{2,\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}&0\\
0&0&X^{2}\otimes I_{N-4}&0\\
0&0&0&X^{1,\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle\mathbf{M}(Y) \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}0&M_{0}(Y)\\
-M_{0}(Y)^{T}&0\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle M_{0}(Y) \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}Y\otimes I_{N-4}&I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{w}\otimes I_{N-4}\\
-I_{2}\otimes A^{(2),\ast}+\overline{\mathbf{w}}\otimes I_{N-4}&Y^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix}. $$

We now expand

$$ \displaystyle|\det[1+\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}+O\left(N^{-\frac{1}{2}+3\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}\right)\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}+O\left(N^{-\frac{1}{2}+3\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}\right)\right\}, $$

where the bound on the third and higher order terms follows by $\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ and $\|\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{C\epsilon_{0}}$ , which we verify immediately below. The second identity follows because $\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})$ has zero diagonal; this can be checked directly. We now collect a few properties of $\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}$ . First, we define the following modification of $\mathbf{M}(Y)$ obtained by replacing $\mathbf{w}$ by $\mathbf{z}=zI_{2}$ :

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y) \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}0&M_{0,z}(Y)\\
-M_{0,z}(Y)^{T}&0\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle M_{0,z}(Y) \displaystyle:=\begin{pmatrix}Y\otimes I_{N-4}&I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}\\
-I_{2}\otimes A^{(2),\ast}+\overline{\mathbf{z}}\otimes I_{N-4}&Y^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}\end{pmatrix}. $$

An elementary computation shows

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)^{-1} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}0&-M_{0,z}(Y)^{-1,T}\\
M_{0,z}(Y)^{-1}&0\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle M_{0,z}(Y)^{-1} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}Y^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(Y)&-[I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}]\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(Y)\\
[I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}]^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(Y)&Y\otimes I_{N-4}\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(Y)\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(Y) \displaystyle=[YY^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}]^{-1} \displaystyle\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(Y) \displaystyle=[Y^{\ast}Y\otimes I_{N-4}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})]^{-1}. $$

Because we restrict to $\|XX^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max},\|X^{\ast}X-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max},\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ for $\delta>0$ small, and because $\eta_{z,t}^{2}\gtrsim N^{-2\epsilon_{0}}$ with $\epsilon_{0}$ small, we know that $\|YY^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max},\|Y^{\ast}Y-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ and thus $\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(Y),H_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(Y)\lesssim\eta_{z,t}^{-2}\lesssim N^{2\epsilon_{0}}$ . This implies $\|\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{C\epsilon_{0}}$ for some $C=O(1)$ with high probability (note that $A^{(2)}$ is bounded in operator norm with high probability; indeed, use interlacing to remove the superscript $(2)$ and by the local law in Lemma 26, for example). On the other hand, we know $\|\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)-\mathbf{M}(Y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1/2}$ locally uniformly in $z_{1},z_{2}$ . Thus, resolvent perturbation shows $\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}=\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)^{-1}[1+O(N^{-1/2+C\epsilon_{0}})]$ , where the big-O is in operator norm. Finally, we define the matrices below obtained by evaluating resolvents at $\eta_{z,t}$ instead of $Y$ :

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}0&-M_{0,z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1,T}\\
M_{0,z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}&0\end{pmatrix} \displaystyle M_{0,z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}Y^{\ast}\otimes I_{N-4}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})&-[I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}]\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\\
[I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}]^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})&Y\otimes I_{N-4}\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}) \displaystyle=[\eta_{z,t}^{2}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}]^{-1} \displaystyle\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}) \displaystyle=[\eta_{z,t}^{2}+(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})^{\ast}(I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4})]^{-1}. $$

Before we proceed, we clarify that $\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})$ is block diagonal with entries $\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{z}(\eta_{z,t})$ and $\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\overline{z}}(\eta_{z,t})$ ; a similar statement holds for $H_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})$ . Thus, its products with $I_{2}\otimes A^{2}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}$ can be analyzed via the local laws in Lemmas 26 and 29. We will use this shortly.

The bounds $\|YY^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max},\|Y^{\ast}Y-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ and resolvent perturbation as before show $\|\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)-\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ and $\|\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)^{-1}-\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}$ . Combining this with $\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}=\mathbf{M}_{z}(Y)^{-1}[1+O(N^{-1/2+C\epsilon_{0}})]$ , we deduce $\|\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}-\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}$ . Also, by the a priori bounds $\|X_{1}\|_{\max},\|X_{2}\|_{\max}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ , we also have the estimate $\|\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim N^{-1/2+\delta}$ . Thus, we have

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}\left({\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}-{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}\right)\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}-\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}]\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}-\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}]\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{O(N^{-\frac{1}{2}+2\delta+C\epsilon_{0}})\right\}, $$

where $\delta,\epsilon_{0}>0$ are small. In particular, we deduce

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}+O\left(N^{-\frac{1}{2}+2\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}\right)\right\}. $$

An elementary computation shows the following, in which $A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z}):=I_{2}\otimes A^{(2)}-\mathbf{z}\otimes I_{N-4}$ , and in which $Y,X^{1},X^{2}$ are identified with $Y\otimes I_{N-4},X^{1}\otimes I_{N-4},X^{2}\otimes I_{N-4}$ , respectively, for convenience:

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2} \displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})X^{1}{H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})\overline{Y}X^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})X^{2,\ast}\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}})^{T}X^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})X^{1}{H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}})X^{1,\ast} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})X^{2,\ast}\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})Y^{T}X^{1,\ast}. $$

Now, observe that $H_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}),\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}),H_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}),\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t}),A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z}),A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}}),A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})^{\ast}$ are all of the form $I_{2}\otimes K$ for some $K\in M_{N-4}(\mathbb{C})$ . Thus, we can factorize the traces on the RHS to get

$$ \displaystyle-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2} \displaystyle=-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}X^{1}\overline{Y}X^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{2,\ast}X^{2} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{1}X^{1,\ast} \displaystyle-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}YX^{2,\ast}Y^{T}X^{1,\ast}. $$

Next, we compute

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}XX^{\ast}\right\}=\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{1}X^{1,\ast}\right\}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{2}X^{2,\ast}\right\}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}YY^{\ast}\right\}. $$

Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}\right\}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}XX^{\ast}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\left(\frac{N}{t}+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}})\right)\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{2,\ast}X^{2}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\left(\frac{N}{t}+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}})\right)\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{1,\ast}X^{1}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}X^{1}\overline{Y}X^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}YX^{2,\ast}Y^{T}X^{1,\ast}\right\} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}YY^{\ast}\right\}. $$

Because $X^{1},X^{2}$ are $2\times 2$ skew-symmetric, we know that ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{2,\ast}X^{2}=2|x_{2}|^{2}$ and ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}X^{1,\ast}X^{1}=2|x_{1}|^{2}$ for $x_{1},x_{2}\in\mathbb{C}$ . Moreover, by the a priori estimate $\|Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\lesssim\eta_{z,t}\lesssim t$ that we restrict to in $\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}}$ , we also know that ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}X^{1}\overline{Y}X^{2}=c_{1}x_{1}x_{2}$ and ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}YX^{2,\ast}Y^{T}X^{1,\ast}=c_{2}\overline{x}_{1}\overline{x}_{2}$ for constants $c_{1},c_{2}=O(\eta_{z,t}^{2})=t^{2}$ . Next, we use Lemma 29 to bound from above both ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})$ and ${\operatorname{Tr}\,}H_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})H_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})$ by $O(N\eta_{z,t}^{-2})$ with high probability. In particular, we deduce

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}Y^{\ast}X^{1}\overline{Y}X^{2}-\frac{1}{2}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t}){\operatorname{Tr}\,}YX^{2,\ast}Y^{T}X^{1,\ast}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{c_{3}x_{1}x_{2}+c_{4}\overline{x}_{1}\overline{x}_{2}\right\}, $$

where $c_{3},c_{4}=O(N)$ . By combining the previous two displays, we obtain

$$ \displaystyle\exp\left\{-\frac{1}{4}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}[\mathbf{M}_{z,\eta_{z,t}}(Y)^{-1}\mathbf{M}(X^{1},X^{2})]^{2}\right\}\exp\left\{-\frac{N}{2t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}XX^{\ast}\right\} \displaystyle=\exp\left\{-\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}\\
x_{2}\end{pmatrix}^{\ast}\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}\\
x_{2}\end{pmatrix}\right\} $$

where $\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})$ is the $2\times 2$ matrix

$$ \displaystyle\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}} \displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},11}&\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},12}\\
\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},21}&\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},22}\end{pmatrix}, \displaystyle\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},11} \displaystyle=\frac{N}{t}+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})^{\ast}{H}^{(2)}_{\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t}){H}^{(2)}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}}), \displaystyle\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},22} \displaystyle=\frac{N}{t}+{\operatorname{Tr}\,}A^{(2)}(\mathbf{z})\tilde{H}_{\mathbf{z}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})\tilde{H}_{\overline{\mathbf{z}}}^{(2)}(\eta_{z,t})A^{(2)}(\overline{\mathbf{z}}), \displaystyle|\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},12}| \displaystyle+|\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},21}|\lesssim N. $$

We now combine (2.37), (2.38), (2.39), (2.40), and (2.41) to deduce

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}} \displaystyle:=\int_{\begin{subarray}{c}\|P-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\mathrm{max}}\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\\
\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-\frac{1}{2}}\end{subarray}}dYe^{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}YY^{\ast}}|\det[\mathbf{M}(Y)]|^{\frac{1}{2}} \displaystyle\times\exp\left\{-\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}\\
x_{2}\end{pmatrix}^{\ast}\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}}(\eta_{z,t})\begin{pmatrix}x_{1}\\
x_{2}\end{pmatrix}\right\}dx_{1}dx_{2}\left\{1+O\left(N^{-\frac{1}{2}+3\delta+C\epsilon_{0}}\right)\right\}. $$

For this, we note the change of variables $dX$ to $dYdx_{1}dx_{2}$ has Jacobian $1$ . Because of the constraints $\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}$ above, we can replace $\|P-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}$ by $\|YY^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}$ in (2.42). Next, by Lemma 29, the on-diagonal terms of $\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}}$ are $\gtrsim Nt^{-1}$ . Thus, $\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z}}\gtrsim Nt^{-1}$ . Since $t=N^{-\epsilon_{0}}$ , we can remove the constraint $\|X^{1}\|_{\max},\|X^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}$ from (2.42) by using the Gaussian weight in the second line. In particular, we can perform the Gaussian integration over $x_{1},x_{2}$ and obtain

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}} \displaystyle=\int_{\|YY^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}}e^{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}YY^{\ast}}|\det[\mathbf{M}(Y)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}|\det\mathbf{T}_{N,t,z}|^{-2}dY\left[1+O(N^{-\kappa})\right] $$

for some $\kappa>0$ . As mentioned earlier, the on-diagonal entries of $\mathbf{T}_{N,t,z}$ are $\gtrsim N^{-1}$ , whereas the off-diagonal entries are $O(N)$ . Thus, for some $\kappa>0$ , we have $\det\mathbf{T}_{N,t,z}=\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},11}\mathbf{T}_{N,t,\mathbf{z},22}[1+O(N^{-\kappa})]=\upsilon_{z,t}^{-2}[1+O(N^{-\kappa})]$ (recall $\upsilon_{z,t}$ from before the statement of this lemma). Therefore, we have

$$ \displaystyle\Upsilon_{\mathrm{main}} \displaystyle=\upsilon_{z,t}^{-2}\int_{\|YY^{\ast}-\eta_{z,t}^{2}\|_{\max}\leq N^{\delta-1/2}}e^{-\frac{N}{t}{\operatorname{Tr}\,}YY^{\ast}}|\det[\mathbf{M}(Y)]|^{\frac{1}{2}}dY\left[1+O(N^{-\kappa})\right]. $$

Now, observe $|\det[\mathbf{M}(Y)]|^{1/2}=\det M_{0}(Y)$ . At this point, we proceed as in Section 5 of [23] to compute the integral in (2.43). Ultimately, after changing variables $Y\mapsto U_{1}SU_{2}^{\ast}$ via singular value decomposition with $U_{1},U_{2}\in\mathbf{U}(2)$ and $S\geq 0$ positive semi-definite, we deduce the following (which is the $\tilde{F}_{0}$ formula in Section 5 of [23]):
